tagline: Korea's gateway city is home to its main international airport, a historic Chinatown and Songdo, a brand-new waterfront district of parks and skyscrapers.
overview: Incheon sits on the Yellow Sea just west of Seoul, and for most travellers it is the first stop in Korea: Incheon International Airport, on reclaimed land off the coast, is one of the busiest in Asia. The city has been a major port since it opened to foreign trade in 1883.

That history shows in Korea's only official Chinatown, founded by Chinese merchants in the late 1800s and the birthplace of jajangmyeon, black-bean noodles. Nearby, the Open Port area keeps old Japanese and Western-style buildings, and Wolmido island has a seaside promenade and amusement rides.

South of the old town, Songdo International Business District was built on reclaimed land in the 2000s. Its Central Park has a seawater canal, and towers like the Northeast Asia Trade Tower rise around it. Offshore, islands such as Ganghwa and Yeongjong add beaches, temples and fortress walls.

funFacts.title: THE GATEWAY TO KOREA
funFacts.text: Incheon International Airport, opened in 2001, is South Korea's main international airport.

funFacts.title: BUILT ON RECLAIMED LAND
funFacts.text: The airport sits on land reclaimed between Yeongjong and Yongyu islands.
